{{Quote|Insects, from a poisonous world. They do not praise their skills or accomplishments, and they are difficult to surprise. They have the instincts of prey, yet are predators&mdash;it is strange.|translated=1|[[Vossk]], a former bounty hunter on Nar Shaddaa, to Meetra Surik|<ref name="KotOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
The '''Gands''', or '''Gand''' {{Pronounced|Gănd}}, were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] believed to have evolved from an [[Insect/Legends|insect]] genus that inhabited the [[Ammonia/Legends|ammonia]]-gas [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Gand (planet)/Legends|Gand]]. Several physical varieties of the species existed, differing from one another in the structure of the head and the texture and [[Color/Legends|color]] of the [[exoskeleton]], but the species was usually divided into two main [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]]: those [[Breather Gand|with]] [[Lung/Legends|lungs]] and those [[Non-breathing Gand/Legends|without]]. Gands with such organs were adapted to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld's]] [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], but like [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dors]], required specialized [[Breath mask/Legends|breathing gear]] if they wanted to leave Gand to manage potentially [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] offworld gas mixtures. Gands without lungs, however, did not respire and were immune to poisonous gases; thus they could venture offworld without worry of suffocation. Both races possessed an exoskeleton and regenerative properties.

Gands were considered by [[Galactic community|galactic society]] to be a very humble species, a trait resultant of their culture, which dictated that an individual's identity had to be earned. Accordingly, most Gands were self-deprecating and polite, and usually referred to themselves in the third person. First-person pronouns were reserved for the most legendary of Gands, as the usage presumed that one was so renowned that everyone knew one's name. However, an accomplished Gand often responded with humility if praised and even downplayed his or her achievements.

Within Gand culture was one of the species' more notable professions: the [[Findsman/Legends|findsmen]]. [[Shaman/Legends|Shamanistic]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], these Gands tracked their quarry by [[The Force/Legends|divining omens]] sent to them via rituals based around the [[Gand religion|religious worship]] of the thick ammonia mists that covered their homeworld. Although their methods were sometimes viewed as arcane, the accuracy of the findsmen was considered unsettling to the casual observer. [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], a bounty hunter, and [[Ooryl Qrygg]], a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] in [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], were two notable Gands.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|At least I know you don't snore. Heck, I don't even know if you breathe.|Corran Horn in regards to rooming with Ooryl Qrygg|<ref name="RS" />}}
Gands, or Gand<ref name="aa" /> ({{Pronounced|Gănd}}),<ref name="NEGtAS" /> were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], stocky [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] whose [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoid]] bodies were covered in a [[Chitin/Legends|chitinous]] [[exoskeleton]].<ref name="CSWE1" /> The natural, durable armor allowed the Gand to shrug off injuries that would cripple most other [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="SAV" /> [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], a Gand [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], jumped from a third-story [[Window/Legends|window]], was caught in an explosion,<ref name="TMA">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref> and was even shot in the shoulder, yet he was able to continue his duties without so much as a disorienting effect.<ref name="YV">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref> The Gand exoskeleton was heavily resistant to blaster fire and other weapons. The Gand exoskeleton provided extra protection in the clavicle region, which prevented most nerve or pressure-point strikes to the neck and shoulders.<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> In addition, Gands had the remarkable ability to regrow lost limbs. If a Gand was [[Dismemberment/Legends|dismembered]], it could regrow a lost limb in a few days. Most Gands usually stood around 1.4 to 1.6 [[Meter/Legends|meters]], and on average weighed 70 to 80 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]],<ref name="SAV" /> although there were some who were even shorter.<ref name="KotOR2" /> Gands, similar to their Kel-Dor cousins, were capable of surviving in the vacuum of space for up to an hour.

The Gands possessed [[Ear/Legends|earholes]],<ref name="HM">''[[Hard Merchandise]]''</ref> and large, compound [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] with a visual range that included the [[Ultraviolet/Legends|ultraviolet]] spectrum<ref name="AE" /> and afforded excellent night vision; however, they could not perceive [[Color/Legends|colors]] in total darkness.<ref name="SAV" /> The eyes were shielded with a [[Keratin/Legends|keratin]] substance that served to protect them from airborne debris, such as that present in a [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorm]].<ref name="AE" /> Most Gands had three fingers on each [[Limb/Legends|hand]]; the digits were capable of punching through [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] armor, and even [[durasteel]], as evidenced by [[Ooryl Qrygg]], a Gand [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] with [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]], on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Talasea]].<ref name="RS" /> Their durability was utilized in a [[Gand martial arts]] technique known as "''Piercing Touch''."<ref name="AE" />

[[File:Vaabesh.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Vaabesh, a Gand Jedi Padawan]]
The Gand species had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]]: male and female.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> Despite the species' refusal to be studied,<ref name="aa" /> [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] managed to document several of their physical variations, which included differences in exoskeleton color from [[Color/Legends|brown]]<ref name="SAV" /> to [[green]],<ref name="RS" /> and [[Color/Legends|purple]].<ref name="TOR" /> Even the shape of the head differed among individuals; some were rounded,<ref name="SAV" /> while others, like [[Vaabesh]], a [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]&ndash;generation Gand [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], possessed elongated craniums.<ref name="BOJ2">[[Republic 56|''Republic'' 56]]</ref> The head in some specimens divided into sections,<ref name="OPF">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> while others had pronounced cranial ridges.<ref name="TM" /> Although most Gands possessed three fingers, there were a few,<ref name="AE" /> like the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[R'Kayza]],<ref name="WHoSaV">''[[Wretched Hives of Scum & Villainy]]''</ref> who had five.<ref name="AE" /> The surface of the exoskeleton varied, as some Gands exhibited pronounced plating,<ref name="Blood Ties">[[Blood Ties 2|''Blood Ties'' 2]]</ref> while others had a smoother texture.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> The eye color also varied from silver<ref name="NEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> to gray,<ref name="BOJ2" /> black,<ref name="JATM" /> yellow,<ref name="SoF">[[Republic 66|''Republic'' 66]]</ref> and turquoise.<ref name="TOR" />

Despite the widespread diversity, however, most Gands were classified into two [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]]: [[Non-breathing Gand/Legends|lungless]] and "[[Breather Gand|breathers]]."<ref name="NEGtC" /> [[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] were unsure if the breathers were of an older evolutionary stock destined to die out or further evolve,<ref name="AE" /> or if they were another viable race.<ref name="EGtAS" /> Such Gands possessed [[Lung/Legends|lungs]], along with the usual assortment of internal organs that were typical in most species.<ref name="SAV" /> The lungs functioned rather efficiently, able to utilize nearly eighty&ndash;five percent of the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] with each breath.<ref name="AE" /> Gands with lungs nevertheless were adapted to breathing only [[Ammonia/Legends|ammonia]] and required [[Breath mask/Legends|breath masks]] or similar equipment to survive in the more common [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]]&ndash;rich environments found on many planets.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> Oxygen exposure scoured the inside of the lungs like [[Acid/Legends|acid]] and required organ transplants if the Gand did not suffocate.<ref name="dns">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050120a|text=We Don't Need That Scum}}</ref> If a Gand survived the initial exposure, that individual could display various respiratory symptoms, which included chest pain, shortness of breath, and coughing, which sometimes brought up [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="OPF" /> Since the proper bronchial and lung treatments necessary to repair the damage were uncommon off the species' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], Gands stricken with oxygen inhalation were characterized by a high rate of mortality.<ref name="AE" />

A breathing Gand was able to hold its breath when needed<ref name="OPF" /> and induce a [[Coma/Legends|comatose]] state,<ref name="DotBH">''[[Aurra Sing: Dawn of the Bounty Hunters]]''</ref> which would reduce the perceptibility of bodily functions to a point where an observer might mistake them for [[Death/Legends|dead]]. Zuckuss demonstrated the ability while working with another bounty hunter named [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]; however, he made use of compressed ammonia canisters to extend respiration cessation for several days.<ref name="SlaveShip">''[[Slave Ship]]''</ref> The lungless Gand sub-species did not respire, as they obtained all the metabolic sustenance they needed through the ingestion of their food.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> Ingested materials aided in gas exchange, and waste passed through openings in the exoskeleton. This made lungless Gands immune to [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] gases and allowed them to forgo respirators when they ventured offworld.<ref name="EGtAS" /> Nevertheless, some lungless Gands wore such equipment anyway, usually to maintain anonymity.<ref name="NEGtAS" />

Usually, Gands spoke their [[Gand (language)/Legends|native language]], also known as Gand,<ref name="SAV" /> which to offworlders sounded like a jumble of drones and clicks.<ref name="TG">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref> For communication with members of other species, however, lungless Gands required the aid of a muscular gas bladder. This organ, among its other uses, allowed the Gand to draw in gases and expel them at a controlled rate through pieces of the exoskeleton that vibrated to approximate speech.<ref name="aa" /> Such Gands also made use of translator [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoders]] to compensate for their lack of vocal cords.<ref name="SAV" /> Although most Gands were incapable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]],<ref name="LAotH">{{FFG|story=The Long Arm of the Hutt|book=Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Beginner Game|text=''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Beginner Game}}</ref> some Gand varieties were born with the proper organs and structure to speak other languages,<ref name="aa" /> Zuckuss being an example.<ref name="Gandspeak">In "[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]", there is no mention of Zuckuss utilizing any vocal assistance, whether a vocoder or a translator, nor is there a mention of his native tongue when he speaks without his gear. In contrast, in''[[Wedge's Gamble]]'', Ooryl Qrygg explains how he speaks. Since there are no indications of Zuckuss utilizing Ooryl's method of speech in "Of Possible Futures," this article assumes that Zuckuss is one of the Basic-speaking Gands mentioned in ''Alien Anthology''.</ref>

Gands needed only a fraction of the [[Sleep/Legends|sleep]] normally required by [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="EGtAS" /> This trait was common throughout the Gand varieties, so scientists attributed it to culture, rather than breeding. To stay awake and aware was more beneficial to the work of [[Findsman/Legends|findsmen]]&mdash;a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] religious tradition of bounty hunters that was unique to the Gand&mdash;and was a skill that was honed throughout a lifetime.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> Some of these findsman could communicate telepathically to all races within 60 meters of them. However, Gands were able to "store" the restorative properties of sleep for use when suspension of consciousness was inadvisable.<ref name="AE" /> Gands possessed regenerative abilities;<ref name="SAV" /> for example, Ooryl Qrygg was able to regrow a severed arm within months, although he was assisted by a [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] cast. The exoskeleton appeared more pale and chalky in hue than normal until the regeneration process was complete.<ref name="RS" /> The consumption of [[Alcohol/Legends|alcohol]] often provoked a depressed mood in the species,<ref name="HM" /> and at least one Gand, Zuckuss, was known to suffer from [[schizophrenia]] and [[multiple personality disorder]].<ref name="EGtAS" /> Gands could also be afflicted with [[asthma]].<ref name="TFU">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Very strange, very quiet.|translated=1|Jekk'Jekk Tarr's [[Unidentified Devaronian bartender|Devaronian bartender]] to the Jedi Exile in regards to the Gand patrons|<ref name="KotOR2" />}}
The Gands evolved on the planet of [[Gand (planet)/Legends|Gand]], an isolated [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world that boasted an atmosphere comprised of ammonia, which made it potentially lethal to oxygen-breathers. This atmosphere resulted in very little [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] influence on the planet, a state of affairs that allowed the Gands to develop a rich, yet peculiar, culture.<ref name="SAV" /> They were considered by most other species to be a very humble society, its members soft-spoken and polite.<ref name="EGtAS" />

Gand society placed heavy importance on the achievements of an individual and held that an individual had no name, and thus no worth, until he or she proved otherwise. The speech patterns of Gands utilized third-person self-reference within each level of identity earned.<ref name="AE" /> Young or unproven Gands were all called "Gand," as they were considered merely aspects of the same whole.<ref name="SAV" /> Major accomplishments earned the use of a family surname.<ref name="EGtAS" /> Mastering a skill, such as becoming a findsman, allowed for the use of the given name, all with third-person self-reference.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> This manner of speaking was common within the spoken and written Gand language<ref name="aa" /> but was more predominant when a Gand spoke Basic;<ref name="RS" /><ref name="OPF" /> it was often a source of amusement to outsiders.<ref name="AE" /> At least one Gand, Ooryl Qrygg, expressed confusion as to what a pronoun was.<ref name="RS" />

[[File:GandJediTwinStrike-JATM.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Gand Jedi during the Clone Wars destroys a [[LR-57 combat droid/Legends|Retail Droid]].]]
A storied Gand could earn the right to use first-person pronouns after many feats and accomplishments and the ritual aptitude test, the ''[[Janwuine-jika]]''.<ref name="TBW">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref> In order for the [[Elders of Gand]]&mdash;the leaders of Gand society&mdash;to deem a Gand worthy to become ''[[janwuine]]'', the highest honor a Gand could receive,<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|139|janwuine}}</ref> they sent the ''[[ruetsavii]]''&mdash;a group of Gands who were renowned for their own accomplishments and therefore considered able to judge the deeds of others<ref name="NEGtAS" />&mdash;to observe and chronicle the exploits of the Gand in question.<ref name="CSWE3">{{CSWECite|III|113|ruetsavii}}</ref> The ''ruetsavii'' then made the determination whether that Gand was ready to undergo the ceremony.<ref name="TBW" /> Use of the first-person self-reference otherwise was considered arrogant, as it implied to those to whom a Gand spoke that he or she was so great that everyone knew his or her name. Once a Gand became ''janwuine'', however, this presumption was considered a reasonable one, as all other Gands were expected to know the individual's name and accomplishments.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> However, even an accomplished Gand warrior often downplayed his or her achievements,<ref name="aa" /> and feelings of shame at one's actions made a Gand assume a reduction of accomplishments, and thus in his or her name. Such name reduction was a show of penance, and depending on the level of identity previously earned, the Gand might take to referring to him- or herself by just the surname or even as "this Gand." Some Gands who committed unspeakable acts were exiled from their society and planet. They were assumed to have discarded their culture and thus could refer to themselves in any way they wished. Failure to become a findsman was sometimes grounds for exile.<ref name="EGtAS" />

The Gands lived in [[Pocket colony|pocket colonies]] that dotted the surface of their homeworld.<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref> These colonies, separated by seemingly endless [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] of thick ammonia mists, were each ruled by Gand's central government.<ref name="FF50">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 50|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 50]]</ref> While some historians believed that the government of the Gand was a totalitarian monarchy, Gands did not possess a word for king or queen in their language, and no royal houses existed in their society. Scholars debated whether monarchies were isolated to colony worlds, if the species had moved away from this form of government, or if the original research into the government was confusing the insect-like characteristics for monarchy. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], sociologists speculated that the Gand might govern themselves in a type of meritocratic democracy. Others theorized that the cultural and political shifts in Gand society were so frequent that the confusion derived from a rapidly changing environment.<ref name="EV">''[[Endless Vigil]]''</ref> The Gands, while a primitive society,<ref name="OFC54">[[Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection 54|''Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection'' 54]]</ref> made use of galactic technology, and were proficient with the usage of advanced weaponry.<ref name="AE" /> However, they either outsourced their [[Starship/Legends|starship]] manufacturing to other companies, such as [[Byblos Drive Yards/Legends|Byblos Drive Yards]],<ref name="OSVC">[[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 8|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 8]]</ref> or heavily modified captured ships, such as was done with the [[Gand starfighter|vehicles]] that were utilized by the ''ruetsavii''.<ref name="TBW" /> The [[Gand discharger]] was a weapon that was considered the pinnacle of Gand technology; dischargers could both paralyze or kill enemies, and they were very rare because few Gand earned them.<ref name="KOTOR 2 Prima">[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

The planet's mists were influential in Gand culture, and the religious findsmen sects worshiped them, divining omens and signs from the currents to pinpoint the location of hidden prey. Gands had an active [[Slavery/Legends|slave trade]] and [[Prison/Legends|penal system]], and they employed the findsmen to locate runaway slaves and prisoners hiding in the enshrouding fog banks.<ref name="GG3" />

The Gands conducted trade and [[Merchant/Legends|commerce]] on orbiting [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] that allowed visitors to avoid the poisonous atmosphere of the planet itself. Despite such contact with offworlders, Gands were seen as insular and somewhat [[Speciesism|xenophobic]]. Outsiders were rarely, if ever, allowed on the surface of Gand, as the insectoid species did not want their society to be tainted with the ideas of independence and self-worth that offworlders might bring.<ref name="SAV" /> The few non-Gand allowed onto the planet were usually under the sponsorship of a ''janwuine'' Gand, or were considered ''[[hinwuine]]''&mdash;beings of standing. Nevertheless, Gand protocol mandated that visitors tell no one of their time on Gand; to talk of such visits was considered an insult to their Gand hosts.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] and several other members of Rogue Squadron were invited onto Gand to witness the ''janwuine-jika'' ceremony for the pilot Ooryl Qrygg. Cracken admitted to finding the ceremony to be unsettling.<ref name="TBW" />

===Findsman===
{{Quote|Fill your enemies with primal fear, then fill their lungs with fire!|Ancient Gand proverb|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>}}
{{Main|Findsman/Legends}}
[[File:GandFindsman.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A Gand findsman with a shockprod staff]]
Within Gand society, a select few felt the call to the path of the findsman.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> The findsmen dated back to ancient times in the Gand society, when certain individuals would demonstrate the ability to find their way between the settlements. This ability was regarded highly within the colonies, and those trackers eventually became known as "findsmen." Over the years, findsmen served as [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] and hunters for their ancient warlords.<ref name="SWKids7">[[Star Wars Kids (1997) 7|''Star Wars Kids'' (1997) 7]] ''Who's that Alien?'' "Gand" entry</ref>

Findsmen belonged to a [[Gand religion|religious sect]] that worshiped and interpreted the movements of the gaseous mists on Gand to predict the location of criminals. Part [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]], part [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcer]], a findsman augured the location of a fugitive, tracked the target, and brought the wanted being to justice. The findsmen rituals were known to take at least three [[Time/Legends|hours]] to complete, but were considered to be very reliable.<ref name="GG3" /> Many offworlders attributed the sect's success to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], believing that findsmen were actually Force-sensitive.<ref name="SAV" /> However, the findsmen themselves claimed otherwise.<ref name="CRO">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref> The title of findsman was sometimes granted to a Gand during the ''janwuine-jika''.<ref name="TBW" />

Individual findsman sects existed within the profession; each held a different set of beliefs regarding its duties and responsibilities, and performed its rituals in its own distinctive way. Findsmen sects also fought with one another, conflicts that usually stemmed from competition over the apprehension of the same target. These skirmishes sometimes escalated into war until another, neutral sect intervened.<ref name="aa" /> Some findsmen groups subjected their pupils to chemical baths and even genetic manipulation to induce the appearance of knob-like growths on specific portions of the exoskeleton.<ref name="EGtAS" /> These serrated ridges, which were often located on the arms and legs and could measure four to five [[Centimeter/Legends|centimeters]] in length,<ref name="AE" /> were used as weapons in hand-to-hand combat.<ref name="EGtAS" /> Gand findsmen also made use of the [[Shockprod staff/Legends|shockprod staff]], an electrical [[Stun/Legends|stun]] weapon that ended in a V-shaped twin prod.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

Findsman training required devotion and study, and to leave the tradition was seen at times as a death sentence for the wayward hunter. If other members of the findsman's sect learned of their initiate's divergence from the path, they often deemed the Gand a rogue and even tried to kill him or her on sight. Members of other species often viewed the findsman tradition to be a strange sect that was devoted to a hunting religion, although the Gands themselves considered the findsmen to be "on the path to truth."<ref name="aa" /> Prior to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the tradition began its decline and many findsmen took their talents offworld.<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> [[Gand shockstaff]]s were developed by Gand Findsmen to help them herd prey&mdash;they had powerful stunning capabilities and a sharp tip.<ref name="KOTOR 2 Prima" />

==History==
{{Quote|They have strange perspectives on life, on hunting, but they are very effective.|translated=1|Vossk|<ref name="KotOR2" />}}
[[File:Gand_FDEV.png|thumb|right|150px|A Gand [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|sentinel]].]]
The Gands evolved on the planet Gand. There, they spread across the surface, founded pocket colonies,<ref name="GG3" /> and developed a planetary monarchy.<ref name="FF50" /> Their homeworld was discovered by outsiders sometime prior to [[3951 BBY]], during the [[Kanz Disorders/Legends|Kanz Disorders]].<ref name="KotOR2" /><ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> An inhospitable and isolated world located in the [[Shadola sector/Legends|Shadola sector]],<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> just beyond the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]] and near the border of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], the planet was not located on any major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]].<ref name="Atlas" /> This isolation allowed the Gand society to develop without the influence of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="OPF" /> During the Clone Wars, aside from the participation of individual members,<ref name="JY">''[[Jedi: Yoda]]''</ref><ref name="JATM" /><ref name="BOJ3">[[Republic 57|''Republic'' 57]]</ref> Gand society remained independent of the Republic.<ref name="Atlas" />

The findsman tradition was established by the planet's monarchy and thrived for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] until the intervention of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Imperials took control of the slave trade and brought with them their advanced technology, which kept the number of runaways down and rendered the findsmen useless.<ref name="OPF" /> Many Gand findsmen retired or tried to find new professions. Two such Gands were the renegade [[Vytor Shrike]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[operative]] [[Venlyss Pnorr]]. However, rather than allow the tradition to face extinction, many other Gands, notably Zuckuss, took the profession offworld, finding work as bounty hunters, security [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]], and even assassins.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="OPF" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Gand homeworld once again had no involvement in the war,<ref name="Atlas" /> aside from the activities of various individuals.<ref name="RS" /><ref name="OPF" /> Aside from the Empire's involvement in the planet's slave trade, the Gands were largely overlooked by the Imperials. The planet managed to avoid invasion during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], as well.<ref name="Atlas" /> Although many Gand refugees sought asylum on [[Ruan]],<ref name="AoC2:JE">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref> the planet itself was overlooked by the [[Yuuzhan Vong|galactic invaders]]. The Gands also remained removed from affairs during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Atlas" />

Since the coming of the Empire, the insular Gands maintained tight control over how much influence outsiders had on their people.<ref name="SAV" /> Most visitors to the planet Gand only got as close as the orbiting space stations. There were five of these structures,<ref name="AE" /> which were the centers of Gand commerce.<ref name="SAV" /> Any visitors permitted on the surface of the world were sequestered in the [[alien quarter]]s located in the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]]. A few non-Gands were afforded the honor of admission into Gand society but only under the sponsorship of the ''janwuine'' or the ''ruetsavii''.<ref name="NEGtAS" /> After the changeover from Galactic Empire to [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the Gands in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="EGtAS" />

==Gands in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Ooryl is token Gand.|Ooryl Qrygg|<ref name="RS" />}}
[[File:DeadlyObservers-EotEBtR.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Gand [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunter]]]]
Gands were a [[Realspace/Legends|space]]-faring species<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref> and those who left their homeworld could be found working in a variety of positions, such as within the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]],<ref name="CSWE4">{{CSWECite|III|287|Vaabesh}}</ref> as bounty hunters,<ref name="aa" /> pilots,<ref name="RS" /> and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]].<ref name="SAV" /> Findsmen who had taken their trade to the wider galaxy often were hired as bounty hunters, security advisors, and assassins.<ref name="GG3" /> Gands were employed by various [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]],<ref name="KotOR2" /> the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]],<ref name="TMA" /><ref name="SoF" /> the Galactic Empire,<ref name="OPF" /> and the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="RS" /> They were found on a number of different planets, such as in the Outer Rim Territories,<ref name="Marked">{{Tales|24|Marked}}</ref> including [[Taris/Legends|Taris]],<ref name="Commencement">[[Knights of the Old Republic 6|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 6]]</ref> [[Dorvalla/Legends|Dorvalla]],<ref name="DMS">"[[Darth Maul: Saboteur]]"</ref> [[Orvax IV]],<ref name="DT:PtN">''[[Star Wars: Dark Times: The Path to Nowhere]]''</ref> and [[Onadax]].<ref name="FHIII">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion]]''</ref> Some Gands made their home on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="TM">''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]''</ref> while others were found on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="EGtAS" /> A Gand warrior who had earned the name [[Ossluk Noslee]] lived sometime before the [[Dark Wars]], and a pair of gloves that were believed to have been owned by him were available for purchase during the Dark Wars.<ref name="KOTOR 2 Prima" />

{{GameLSmechanics}}
During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a Gand named [[Aulus G'luun]] led a group of Gand [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] on Coruscant, where he had come to feel that the Gands were victims of discriminatory laws and lack of opportunity. Seeing no other choice, G'luun agreed to work with [[Lars Baddeg]], a leader of a criminal organization known as the [[Migrant Merchants' Guild]], who asked him to keep a [[Jedi artifact/Legends|Jedi artifact]]&mdash;the [[Noetikon]]&mdash;safe and out of Jedi hands. The group adopted a complex system whereby computerized signals told when to pass the device off from one Gand to another. However, when Republic security forces spotted a Gand carrying the stolen device, they barricaded the Guild to prevent the Gands from escaping the planet and captured [[Unidentified Gand scavenger|one]] of G'luun's underlings. A [[The Barsen'thor|Jedi Consular]] interrogated the captured Gand on a mission to recover the [[Noetikon of Science|Noetikon]], which held important information regarding the afflicted [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yuon Par]]. Using the Gand scavenger's information, the Jedi activated the signal device in the [[Old Galactic Market]] and attracted G'luun's attention. The Jedi convinced the Gand leader that the barricade would be removed and the Gands permitted to leave Coruscant if he handed over the Noetikon, so G'luun complied.<ref name="Secret Signals">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Secret Signals|Coruscant}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

A large number of offworld Gands found work as bounty hunters<ref name="aa" /> or [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]]. One group of Gands with pink carapaces served under the exiled [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Tytonus]] of [[Begeren]]. The Gand enforcers accompanied Tytonus's private [[Army/Legends|army]] to the jungle beyond the lowest levels of the [[Kaas City]] [[Kaas City expansion district|expansion district]] on the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] throne world of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] during the Cold War. Before the force could mount their invasion of Dromund Kaas, however, a group of Imperial operatives assaulted their position and destroyed their [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]], which stymied Tytonus's plans.<ref name="Friends of Old">{{TORcite|type=heroic|Friends of Old|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> A number of Gands were imprisoned on the planet [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] by the Republic, and a group of them were forced to participate in [[Project Noble Focus]]&mdash;combat experiments to determine the combat capabilities of various species. When the Sith Empire [[Invasion of Belsavis|attacked]] Belsavis, the Gands were among the prisoners who were freed in the chaos, and they kidnapped several Republic scientists before retreating to a [[Gand vault|Rakatan vault]] in the [[High Security Section]]. The group was led by two Gands named [[Zyyskel]] and [[Naarud Nyydo]], but Republic forces eventually stormed the vault and rescued the scientists.<ref name="Lesson">{{TORcite|type=heroic|A Lesson is Learned|Belsavis}}</ref>

Since then, many Gands&mdash;primarily a group of bounty hunters who left to live on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]&mdash;regularly visited [[Jekk'Jekk Tarr]], an exotic [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] where they could find gas fumes similar to those present on their homeworld. Later, a group of Gands that were members of the same [[Gand nest|nest]] as the Jekk'Jekk Tarr group was present on the ''[[Visionary]]'', a [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]] that belonged to [[G0-T0]], the leader of a criminal organization known as the [[Exchange]].<ref name="KotOR2" /> Many of them were killed by [[Meetra Surik]]&mdash;a Human woman<ref name="KotORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> who chose to disobey the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] and aid the Republic in the [[Mandalorian Wars|war]] against the invading [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Neo-Crusaders]]&mdash;first during her search for the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] Exchange crime lord, [[Visquis]], and later when the Exile stormed the ''Visionary'' to defeat G0-T0.<ref name="KotOR2" /> A [[Unidentified Gand bounty hunter (Ord Mantell)|Gand bounty hunter]] was present on [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] during the hunt for the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]].<ref name="RoP">[[Star Wars (1998) 43|''Star Wars'' (1998) 43]]</ref> [[Unidentified Gand bounty hunter (The Rig)|Another Gand]] hunter was present on [[the Rig]] shortly after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], when Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] arrived seeking information on who in the Bounty Hunters' Guild was responsible for the [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] posted on Jedi. This particular hunter was killed by Windu in the resulting [[Mission to the Rig|scuffle]].<ref name="SoF" /> A [[Unidentified Gand bounty hunter (Connor Freeman)|Gand bounty hunter]] attempted to collect a bounty on [[Connor Freeman]], who was wanted by an individual named [[Tayand]] for beating the crime lord at a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], but this Gand failed after being felled by a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] shot from Freeman.<ref name="Blood Ties" />

[[File:EotE_Gand_bounty_hunter_by_Palmer.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], a Gand [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]]]
After the Clone Wars, since the intervention of the Empire on their homeworld's slave trade, many former findsmen took their trade off-world, where they were able to find employment in a variety of agencies. Such findsmen included Zuckuss,<ref name="GG3" /> a bounty hunter who was known in the trade as "the Uncanny One," due to his abilities. He often partnered with [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] bounty hunter.<ref name="OPF" /> He was considered to be one of the best Gand findsmen,<ref name="SWK">{{Kids1997Cite|10|Meet...|Meet Boba Fett!}}</ref> and his talents brought him to the attention of the Bounty Hunters' Guild,<ref name="HtOHH">{{GamerCite|6|How the Other Half Hunts}}</ref> the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]],<ref name="FF61">{{FactFile|61|BOU 15-16|Bounty Hunters &ndash; Zuckuss}}</ref> the Galactic Empire and even the Rebel Alliance for a time. Zuckuss's career had seen some upsets; during the Galactic Civil War, he had suffered a life-threatening lung injury and while acquiring the necessary [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to afford an organ transplant, he accepted a job with the Rebellion to track down Imperial [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Nardix]]. His involvement in the affair resulted in death warrants being posted for both him and 4-LOM, though those postings were overlooked when the pair were contracted to hunt down the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] shortly after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].<ref name="OPF" />

Soon afterward, Zuckuss and 4-LOM defected to the Rebel Alliance, where Zuckuss received the necessary medical treatment to repair his oxygen-burned lungs.<ref name="OPF" /> He was later involved in a mission to reclaim the [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]-encased [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] from rival hunter Boba Fett.<ref name="NEGtC" /> The mission, however, was a failure, and after the destruction of 4-LOM,<ref name="SotE5">[[Shadows of the Empire 5|''Shadows of the Empire'' 5]]</ref> Zuckuss left the Rebellion to concentrate on rebuilding his partner. 4-LOM, after having received a [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]], lost his loyalties to Zuckuss and intended to work alone.<ref name="HtOHH" /> Zuckuss managed to convince the droid to partner together for one last hunt,<ref name="HM" /> though they soon parted ways, with Zuckuss relocating to the Outer Rim.<ref name="HtOHH" /> Due to his Alliance sympathies, Zuckuss began to take primarily New Republic contracts.<ref name="HoD">{{GamerCite|7|Harbingers of Doom}}</ref> He was later incarcerated in a penal facility on Coruscant, where he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and multiple personality disorder.<ref name="EGtAS" />

Zuckuss's second-cousin and fellow findsman, [[Lu'daal-ud]], worked for the [[Granse Confederacy]], which was a coalition of bounty hunters and trackers that was formed shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> Another findsman, [[Vaskau Farg]], had once tracked a [[Sakiyan/Legends|Sakiyan]] witch to the planet [[Arkania/Legends|Arkania]].<ref name="AC">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030206arkanianintro|text=Arkanian Chill|int=Arkanian Chill}}</ref> Vytor Shrike was an active bounty hunter on Tatooine, and at some point, he joined a group of freedom fighters who were led by [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]], a renowned military [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] tactician and [[Navy/Legends|naval]] commander.<ref name="TM" /> Venlyss Pnorr worked under the guise of being a hunter and transported Rebel Alliance operatives to safehouses. After a mission ended with the death of one of his charges, Pnorr went into hiding.<ref name="CRO" /> Another Gand Findsman who found work as a bounty hunter was [[Vrixx'tt]], who attempted to negotiate a weapons contract with the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Piddock]] on behalf of a group of Gand bounty hunters.<ref name="LAotH" />

There were some Gands who pursued what most considered to be nobler professions, such as serving with the Jedi Order.<ref name="CSWE4" /> Vaabesh, an orphaned Padawan during the waning years of the Galactic Republic, served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]] for the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]].<ref name="BOJ2" /> However, he lost his life during the [[Battle of Jabiim|Second Battle of Jabiim]] in 21 BBY.<ref name="BOJ3" /> Another Gand, Jedi Master [[Tyffix]], served as a general for the Galactic Republic. During the [[Battle of Thustra]], he sacrificed his life to save those of his and Master [[Tyr]]'s Padawans when their [[Thustra Republic command center|command center]] was struck by a [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]].<ref name="JY" /> During the time of the Galactic Republic, Gands worked in such professions as merchants, such as [[Qoussk]], a Gand who operated a specialty goods kiosk on Coruscant, and [[Yuun (Gand)|Yuun]], a findsman, was employed as a [[Technician/Legends|technician]] with the [[Republic Army]].<ref name="TOR" />

[[File:OorylQrygg-JP.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[Ooryl Qrygg]], sans ubiquitous [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]], a pilot for [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]]]]
During the Galactic Civil War, another Gand, Ooryl Qrygg, served as a pilot for the newly-reformed Rogue Squadron. Through learning how to pilot a ship, Ooryl was granted the right to refer to himself by his surname, Qrygg. After he mastered advanced flight training and [[Astrogation/Legends|astrogation]], he was able to use his given name. Ooryl was present on Talasea, where he used his martial arts training to help counter a raid on the Rebel base. He also participated in an abortive mission to [[Borleias/Legends|Borleias]], where Rogue Squadron hoped to capture the planet codenamed [[Blackmoon]]. If the mission was successful, it was hoped by the Rebel fleet that the location could be used as a staging point for capturing Coruscant. However, due to a breakdown in [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] intelligence, the Rebels missed the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] squadrons that were stationed in the [[Alderaan Biotics]] facility. In the resulting battle, Ooryl lost his arm after he was ejected from his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]]. With the usage of a bacta cast, Ooryl was able to regenerate his arm at an accelerated rate.<ref name="RS" /> He had recovered in time to participate in a mission to potentially liberate Coruscant. Due to his biology, Ooryl was able to pass unaffected through a nerve gas-congested area in a subsidiary computer center, where he retrieved breathing equipment for his squadmates.<ref name="WG">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>

In 7 ABY, a trio of ''ruetsavii'' Gands, [[Syron Aalun]], [[Ussar Vlee]], and [[Vviir Wiamdi]], were sent to observe Qrygg and aided in several raids during the [[Bacta War]], a conflict that stemmed from the conquest of [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]] and subsequent retaliation by Rogue Squadron in the [[Battle of Thyferra]]. Ooryl was deemed to have attained sufficient heroic status and after undergoing the ''janwuine-jika'' ritual, he was granted the right to refer to himself in first person.<ref name="TBW" /> Ooryl fought in the [[Thrawn campaign]] and was an active squadron member during the liberation of the [[Ciutric Hegemony]], following the resurrection of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="IR">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref> He unknowingly faced off against fellow pilot [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] and was left adrift until he was rescued and returned to the fleet. Alongside [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], Qrygg also used his findsman talents to track down Horn while the latter was undercover. The trio later stormed the [[Jensaarai/Legends|Jensaarai]] fortress on [[Susevfi]] and freed [[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax Terrik]], Corran's wife, from captivity.<ref name="IJ">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> At a later date, Ooryl attended the wedding of Luke Skywalker and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]].<ref name="Union">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref>

Gands were seen on Taris as early as [[3964 BBY]]; one was present when suspected [[Padawan Massacre|murderer]] and former Padawan [[Zayne Carrick]] returned to the planet.<ref name="Commencement" /> Tarisian Gands also participated in [[Sok Brok's Fiftieth Annual Pet Show]], in [[43 ABY]], when Gand pet owners displayed their domesticated animals in the "Insectoid" division.<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref> Another Gand, [[Ossluk Noslee]], was a prominent warrior who had earned two names as testimony of his accomplishments; a pair of [[Ossluk's gloves|his]] [[Glove/Legends|gloves]] had survived into the period of the [[Dark Wars]].<ref name="KotOR2" /> Gands were also seen in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]] in a cantina on Dorvalla,<ref name="DMS" /> a planet in the Outer Rim Territories;<ref name="Marked" /> they were also present on the slave trade planet Orvax IV.<ref name="DT:PtN" /> Some Gands allied themselves with smugglers, such as [[Unidentified Gand (Scarlet Vertha)|the Gand]] who served as a crewmember on the [[Scarlet Vertha/Legends|''Scarlet Vertha'']], a custom-made ship owned by the [[Morseerian/Legends|Morseerian]] [[Nabrun Leids/Legends|Nabrun Leids]].<ref name="SotSR">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> Other Gands worked as smugglers themselves<ref name="SAV" /> or, like R'Kayza, found employment as assassins.<ref name="WHoSaV" /> In [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]], [[Unidentified Gand (Onadax)|another Gand]] was seen in a cantina on the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]] planet of Onadax.<ref name="FHIII" /> During the pan-galactic Yuuzhan Vong War, to elude capture or destruction by the invading Yuuzhan Vong, many Gands had taken refuge in the squalid [[Refugee Facility 17]] that had been established on the planet Ruan.<ref name="AoC2:JE" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|When you come from a planet like Gand, where we've got both ammonia-breathers and oxygen-breathers, you have to be adaptable.|Zuckuss to [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], in regards to species biology|<ref name="SlaveShip" />}}
Zuckuss's appearance with the bounty hunters on board the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]], the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] in [[1980]] marked the first appearance of his then-unnamed insectoid species. Portrayed by actress [[Cathy Munro|Catherine Monroe]], the character's features were designed by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] and [[John Mollo]], and the mask was crafted by [[Stuart Freeborn]]. The compound eyes of the mask were constructed with [[Wikipedia:Bubble wrap|bubble wrap]] packing material. The costume itself consisted of the full-head mask and attached cylinders that were filled with colored water, and the actress was instructed to blow air into the cylinders in order to create bubbles.<ref name="MunroeInterview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsaficionado.com/f/CATHERINE_MUNROE_INTERVIEW1.pdf|text=Interview with Catherine Munroe on Star Wars Aficionado|format=.pdf|archivedate=20130927184813}}</ref>

[[File:ZuckussConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept art of Zuckuss by John Mollo]]
Zuckuss's species was given a name in [[1989]] with the publication of [[West End Games]]' [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back|first edition]] of ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', written by [[Michael Stern]]. Since then, however, the species name has encountered various misspellings, including "Gann" in ''[[Star Wars Missions 11: Bounty Hunters vs. Battle Droids]]'' in [[1998]], and in [[2008]] with "Gund" on the packaging for the [[Kotobukiya]] ArtFX Zuckuss statue.<ref name="ArtFX">{{Amazon|url=Kotobukiya-Star-Zuckuss-ArtFX-Statue/dp/B0013NAL5M|text=Kotobukiya Star Wars Zuckuss ArtFX Statue}}</ref> Throughout the source material, the usage of the Gand plural form varies between "Gands" and "Gand." The former was used in [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] and its [[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species|successor]], whereas [[Wizards of the Coast]] sources, such as ''[[Alien Anthology]]'' and the ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', used "Gand" as both singular and plural. The [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 15|''Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 15]] suggested that the findsmen religious sect was instead a sub-species; as this conflicts with all other sources that describe the findsmen, this article assumes ''The Official Starship & Vehicles Collection'' is in error.

Aside from source material such as ''Galaxy Guide 3'', the species' first foray into the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] was in [[January 1]], [[1996]], in the novel ''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]'' by [[Michael A. Stackpole]], with the introduction of the character of Ooryl Qrygg. This novel also introduced the previously undocumented lungless sub-species. In [[December]] of that same year, ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'' was released, which featured the short story ''[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]'', written by [[M. Shayne Bell]]. The short story utilized sources from West End Games, which at the time made no mention of the lungless Gand sub-species.

In ''[[Slave Ship]]'', the second book of ''[[The Bounty Hunter Wars]]'' trilogy by [[K. W. Jeter]], the character Zuckuss claims his species has "both ammonia-breathers and oxygen-breathers." As no other sources mention oxygen breathers, but many assert the atmosphere of Gand to be ammonia, this article treats this statement by Zuckuss as a mistaken reference to lungless Gands.

Gand characters feature in the online [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', released by [[BioWare]] in [[2011]]. In one quest, "Secret Signals" on Coruscant, the Jedi Consular player character has the option to use the Force to [[Mind trick/Legends|persuade]] both a captured Gand scavenger and the Gand scavenger leader, Aulus G'luun, or to simply attack them to retrieve a stolen Noetikon. However, Force persuasion prevents the player character from helping the Gands and thus obviates the ability to earn affinity for the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]], while attacking them moves the character toward the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Therefore, talking to the Gands and solving their problems is considered here to be the canonical outcome. Similarly, when the Jedi Consular chooses from three signals to attract the Gands and retrieve the Noetikon they are keeping, two options simply attract enemy characters known as "Gand Protectors", with whom the player character can only fight, not communicate. Although such an outcome secures the Noetikon and finishes the mission, only peacefully dealing with the Gand leader Aulus G'luun directly and convincing him to turn over the Noetikon grants the player greater affinity to the light side. Thus, this article treats such an outcome as canonical.<ref name="Secret Signals" />
